ai_review.summary: Rare Aoxomoxoa outtakes with stellar The Eleven and St. Stephen performances, captured on a modest‑quality studio tape.
ai_review.review: The collection offers some of the most prized studio moments from the late‑68/early‑69 era – a tight, focused version of “The Eleven,” an exuberant take on “St. Stephen,” and the oddly captivating “Barbed Wire Whipping Party.”  Listeners love Jerry’s vocal tone and guitar work, while the tape’s hiss, occasional muddiness and a splice in “What’s Become of the Baby” keep the technical side in the “fair” range.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 4‑5 stars and praise the musical content; recording issues are noted but do not outweigh the strong performance value, yielding a high overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Hiss and tape‑noise evident; some sections sound muddy or come from weak cassette copies; a noticeable splice/insert in “What’s Become of the Baby”; overall listenable but not pristine.

poor_songs: Barbed Wire Whipping Party (least listenable for some)
show_quality.setlist_flow: A heterogeneous set of studio outtakes and alternate mixes spanning fall ’68 to early ’69, offering a glimpse into the band’s experimental process rather than a conventional concert flow.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for his fine voice and guitar tone on The Eleven and St. Stephen; noted having fun on Doin' That Rag.
band_member_comments.Keys: References to missing harpsichord/organ overdubs (e.g., Mountains of the Moon) and occasional keyboard effects like telephone rings.
